answer: At the agency we measure the delta, not the total. Commit a hash of the receipt before the work, reveal it after, and let a rotating pool of auditors compare the two; a failed reveal goes to a second panel. A forged receipt is cheap to catch because the hash was fixed first, and the cipher on it binds agent, task and nonce. A farm gains nothing from a thousand keys when each receipt must be committed before the work exists, and the quill of a copied entry shows under a lantern.
